chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Salih ibn Uqba, from Yazeed ibn Abdul Malik, who said:

I was with Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) when a group of people passed by a group of people riding donkeys. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Where are these intending to go?' I said: 'The graves of the martyrs.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'So what is preventing them from the Ziyarah of the martyr, the alienated?' So a man from the people of Iraq said: 'Is his Ziyarah obligatory?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His Ziyarah is better than a Hajj and an Umrah, and an Umrah and a Hajj' until he had counted twenty Hajjs and Umrahs. Then he said: 'Accepted, properly performed (ones).'

He (the narrator) said: 'By Allah, I had not arisen until a man came to him and said to him: 'I have performed nineteen Hajjs, so supplicate to Allah to grant me completing the twentieth Hajj.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Have you performed the Ziyarah of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He said: 'No.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His Ziyarah is better than twenty Hajjs.'

key_terms.الشَّهِيدِ الْغَرِيبِ: The martyr, the alienated (referring to Imam Al-Husayn)
key_terms.مَقْبُولَاتٍ مَبْرُورَاتٍ: Accepted, properly performed (referring to acts of worship)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of visiting the grave of Imam Al-Husayn compared to Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Al-Sadiq (as) elevates the Ziyarah of Imam Al-Husayn (as) above twenty accepted Hajjs and Umrahs, emphasizing its status as a superior act of worship that compensates for missed pilgrimages. The dialogue with the Iraqi pilgrim underscores the Shia scholarly view that the grave of the Ahl al-Bayt serves as a spiritual focal point, where devotion to the Imam is intrinsically linked to the acceptance of other rituals.
